title: openai: /v1/chat.completions parity — roles, stop, logprobs, streaming, function-calls, structured output
author: Ayesha Patel
description: Add OpenAI /v1/chat.completions parity for roles, stop, logprobs, response formatting, streaming stability, and function/tool calling. This PR implements the compatibility layer that accepts OpenAI-style parameters and maps them to Redwood's internal chat API while preserving semantics for streaming tokens, assistant/system/user roles, stop sequences, and logprobs support. Motivation: customers expect drop-in compatibility with existing OpenAI client codebases and tooling. Scope: parameter parsing/validation, runtime mapping for streaming vs non-streaming paths, structured output (JSON/format enforcement), function-calling hook integration, and compatibility test suite. The implementation includes: 1) request parsing layer that accepts messages with role fields and OpenAI parameter names (temperature, top_p, n, max_tokens, stop, logprobs, stream, functions, function_call). 2) Deterministic mapping to Redwood route configs and model selection, with explicit fallbacks when a feature (e.g., per-token logprobs) is unsupported by a model or quantized variant. 3) Streaming stability improvements: resilient chunk reassembly, explicit per-chunk seq numbers to avoid duplication on reconnects, and backpressure alignment with client stream events. 4) Function/tool calling: accept OpenAI functions schema, transform to internal tool registry invocation, preserve function metadata in streaming function call breadcrumb events, and support automatic function selection in the runtime. 5) Structured output validation: JSON schema enforcement for assistant responses when users request structured format, with graceful fallbacks and clear error messages. 6) Tests: end-to-end compatibility tests against representative OpenAI client calls, unit tests for parsing and mapping, and integration tests exercising streaming failure/recovery. Backwards compatibility: default behavior for existing Redwood clients unchanged; OpenAI compatibility opt-in via api_path /v1/chat.completions or a compatibility header. Rollout: staged on canary, with feature flag openai_compat that can be toggled per-customer. See release_notes for migration notes and known limitations.
commits: feat(openai-compat): add request parsing and mapping for chat.completions
feat(streaming): resilient chunk reassembly and seq numbering for stream stability
feat(functions): wire OpenAI 'functions' schema into tool selection pipeline
fix(tests): add compatibility test vectors and flaky stream replay test
docs(openai): update API docs and migration guide

release_notes: Adds an OpenAI /v1/chat.completions compatibility endpoint. Supports roles, stop sequences, logprobs, streaming, function/tool calls, and structured output validation. Default Redwood behavior unchanged; opt-in via /v1/chat.completions path or 'OpenAI-Compat' header. Feature launched behind flag openai_compat for staged rollout.
known_limitations: Per-token logprobs are best-effort and may be unavailable for quantized models; in that case a clear warning is returned and logprobs=nil. Function selection uses heuristic ranking; full canonical OpenAI behavior for ambiguous cases is not guaranteed on initial rollout.
migration_guide: Users can switch by using the new endpoint /v1/chat.completions. If you rely on deterministic per-token logprobs or exact OpenAI function resolution behavior, test against the openai_compat fixture. For streaming clients, expect a small change: streams now include chunk_seq numbers and a final 'done' event to simplify reconnection handling.
changelog_entry: OpenAI compatibility: add /v1/chat.completions parity for roles, stop, logprobs, streaming, and function-calls (opt-in behind openai_compat flag).
qa_notes: Manual QA run executed against canary region; simulated network interruptions to validate stream reconnection and deduplication. Observability added: streaming.reassembly.duplicates metric and openai_compat.request_count tag.
